# Start Stories Script: every scene of the ten character starts

Generated by `tools/probes/StoryDump.java` from the source. Read it from top to bottom; mark what to change. The words are exactly the game's, with the placeholders left in: `{name}` / `{first}` / `{last}` the player, `{key}` / `{key.first}` a person of the story, `{@place}` a place of the story, `{#flag}` a number. A line marked *[only if ...]* shows only when you made that choice (or that person is dead).

How a chapter runs: a window with the **opening scene** (and sometimes a question), then a **task** (it sits in the Quest Log as `Story: ...`), then the **closing scene** (sometimes another question), then the reward. The next chapter starts once its *Starts when* is true. **"Make N items" is a real task** (a count of what you craft); **"Wait"** and **"No task"** chapters ask nothing of you but time.

# 1. The Last Heir of the Azure Cloud Sect  (`heir`)

*Your sect burned, your master's last gift was a cracked cauldron and a name to find. You are the best talent in a generation, and everyone who ruined your home knows it.*

Starts as: any, trait Alchemist, Neutral, potential 100, 500 spirit stones.

**What the plan says is the truth of this story:** The Last Heir of the Azure Cloud Sect (12 chapters). The hand that burned the sect was Cinder Wraith, raised in Marrow Reach; the man who paid him was the kind Magistrate Orrin Vale; the reason was the sect's Silent Tonic, made of a root that Orrin's agents dug out of Marrow Reach until the water killed the village. Master Hui learned it, refused another batch and wrote that he would tell the Court; Orrin burned the sect a week before. [Wen Sorrel, Orrin Vale, Cinder Wraith, Pell Wraith]. Choices: mercy (Marrow Reach), patron (Orrin's money), kill or spare Cinder, how to end Orrin (expose / duel / take his offer), what the cauldron is for. If Cinder is killed, his ward Pell comes for revenge twenty years later and may have killed Wen first; if he is spared, he writes from the south.

# 1.S1  Season 1: Ash

## 1.1  "Ash"  (`ash`)

- **Starts when:** the first week of the story
- **Task:** Reach Major Lvl 1.  "Awaken your cultivation: reach Major Lvl 1."
- **Pays:** 3 Cultivation Pills
- **Words:** 293 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The fire is a week old. You can still smell it in your hair.

You are eighteen. You have a cracked cauldron, a few coins, and no home.

Azure Cloud was a small sect. It made cheap pills for fevers and farm cough. It had forty people, a herb garden, and one fat kitchen cat. Now it is a black field with one chimney standing in the middle.

You were at the market when it burned. You saw the smoke from the road and ran the whole way. By the gate there was nothing left to save. Only Master Hui, pinned under a kitchen beam, still breathing.

**Hui:** Take the cauldron. It is cracked, but it is all I could carry out.

**Hui:** Do not chase the man with the torch. He is only a hand. Find the one who gave him the match.

**You:** Who? Who gave it to him?

Master Hui tried to say a name. It sounded like 'Vale,' or maybe 'valley.' Then his hand went slack.

You buried him in the herb garden, where he liked to sit. You did not cry until the grave was finished.

Now the cauldron sits heavy in your arms. Someone burned your home. Someone paid for it. You mean to find out who.

But you are a pill-maker who has barely begun to cultivate. First you must become someone who can ask questions and stay alive.

**Closing scene**

It is a small thing, the first gate. Something inside you clicks, like a latch lifting.

You think of Master Hui, who used to say that strength is only patience wearing armor.

Then you think of the torch, and the patience has to be held down with both hands.

## 1.2  "The Blue Cloud"  (`wen`)

- **Starts when:** 1 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; Major Lvl 1 or more (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** Meet wen (walk to their tile).  "Find the herb seller in {@wen}."
- **Pays:** 300 spirit stones
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "wen")`
- **Words:** 233 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

A year goes by. You brew pills, you sell pills, and you ask careful questions in a careless voice.

Then a traveling herbalist tells you something odd over a cup of cheap tea.

**Herbalist:** There's a {wen.man} in {@wen} who sells herbs with a blue cloud stitched on {wen.his} sleeve.

A blue cloud. Your heart does something clumsy in your chest.

**Closing scene**

{wen.He} drops {wen.his} basket. Mint and sage roll across the cobbles. {wen.He} does not pick them up.

**Wen:** You're not dead... I counted the bodies... You weren't there, but I couldn't find you...

{wen.He} hugs you hard enough to hurt. {wen.He} smells of crushed leaves and cheap soap, and for a moment you are twelve years old again.

**Wen:** I was in the next valley picking nightbloom. I saw the smoke from the hill. I ran down, but it was too late.

**Wen:** I saw one thing. A rider on the north road, going fast. Grey cloak.

**Wen:** In the south they call him Cinder Wraith. He's a hired blade. Everyone knows the name, but nobody knows who hires him.

{wen.He} presses a scrap of paper into your palm. It is a page from the sect ledger, burned black at the edges.

**Wen:** I took it from the gatehouse. I can't make sense of it. Maybe you will, someday.

You do not let go of {wen.his} sleeve for a long time.

## 1.3  "The Cracked Cauldron"  (`lid`)

- **Starts when:** 1 year(s) after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Make 10 items **since this chapter began**.  "Brew in the old cauldron: make ten items."
- **Pays:** gear a Major above you
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.set(st, "craft0", c.itemsCrafted)`
- **Words:** 165 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

You and Wen share a small room above a noodle shop. The cauldron sits in the corner, cracked from rim to belly. Neither of you can look at it for long.

**Wen:** Master Hui used to say a cauldron learns the hand that stirs it.

**You:** It's cracked. It leaks.

**Wen:** So patch it with clay and cook slowly. Make something. Anything. I'm tired of looking at it like a gravestone.

So you do. Ten brews, one after another.

**Closing scene**

On the tenth night the clay patch loosens in the heat. Under it, scratched into the iron, are words you never saw in all your years at Azure Cloud.

'Marrow Reach. Silent Tonic. Forgive me.'

**Wen:** I never heard of a Silent Tonic.

Neither had you. It is Master Hui's handwriting. He pressed hard, as if he wanted the iron to remember what he could not say.

**Wen:** Marrow Reach is a swamp village. Nobody goes there. Why would Master Hui be sorry about a swamp?

## 1.4  "A Kind Letter"  (`letter`)

- **Starts when:** 2 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; Major Lvl 2 or more (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** Meet orrin (walk to their tile).  "Visit Magistrate Orrin Vale in {@vale}."
- **Pays:** nothing
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "orrin")`
- **When it closes, the code:** `(c, st) -> { if (Chapters.flag(st, "patron") == 1) { c.ss += 3000; c.convertCurrency(); } }`
- **Words:** 190 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

A letter arrives, sealed in green wax with a leaf crest. Wen reads it over your shoulder and whistles.

'I knew your master well, and I have grieved for him these many years. I hear you are rising. Let me help you rebuild. My door is open, and so is my purse. Orrin Vale, Magistrate of {@vale}.'

**Wen:** A magistrate wants to help us. That is either very good or very strange.

**You:** Master Hui never mentioned him.

**Wen:** Master Hui never mentioned a lot of things.

**Closing scene**

Orrin Vale is nothing like a magistrate in a story. He is round and warm, with ink on his fingers and a robe that smells of cedar. He pours the tea himself.

**Orrin:** Hui and I talked for hours, in the old days. He never stopped talking about his students. You, mostly. You burned the sugar pills, he said, and cried about it.

You laugh before you can stop yourself. It is true.

**Orrin:** I can't give back what was taken. But I can give you a start. Three thousand spirit stones, and a seat at my table whenever you are in the province.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `patron`; default: option 1)

> Orrin offers you three thousand spirit stones. What do you do?

1. Accept, and thank him.
   - **Orrin:** Good. Hui would have wanted it. Don't be a stranger.
   - The purse is heavy and the tea is good, and you feel a little less alone.
2. Thank him, but refuse the money.
   - **Orrin:** Proud, like your master. Fine. The invitation stands, and it costs you nothing.
   - You walk out with empty hands. Oddly, you feel lighter.

## 1.5  "Marrow Reach"  (`marrow`)

- **Starts when:** 3 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; Major Lvl 3 or more (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** Go to the place `marrow`.  "Go to Marrow Reach, at {@marrow}."
- **Pays:** a technique insight
- **Words:** 263 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The words in the cauldron will not leave you alone. You ask in taverns. You ask in libraries. A mapmaker finally answers, and she looks uneasy doing it.

**Mapmaker:** Marrow Reach? It's a swamp hamlet at {@marrow}. Poor soil, bad water. The roads have grown over. People say there was a sickness there, years back. Nobody asks.

You fold the map slowly. Forgive me, the iron said.

**Closing scene**

There is no village left. There are reeds, and low mounds under the reeds, and a ring of leaning posts that might once have been a fence.

An old woman sits on a stump with a pole across her knees. She watches you the way you watch weather.

**Old woman:** Azure Cloud. I know that sleeve. The old man wore it.

**You:** Master Hui came here?

**Old woman:** Three winters after. He brought a cart of grain and he knelt in the mud. We did not forgive him. He came back every spring until the spring he didn't.

**You:** Forgive him for what?

**Old woman:** For the root. Bitterbell. It grows here and nowhere else. Men came with silver and a contract, and they dug it by the cartload and washed it in the creek. Within a year the water turned. Sixty of us died. My daughter. Her little brother lived, because she carried him out.

**Old woman:** Your sect made the tonic and the magistrate's agents bought the root. Everyone ate, but nobody asked where the meal came from.

She spits into the reeds. Not at you. Near you.

**Old woman:** Your old man asked too late. That is more than most did.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `mercy`; default: option 1)

> What do you make of what you heard?

1. They had every right to be angry.
   - You bow to the old woman. She does not bow back, but she does not look away either. 'Sit,' she says, 'before you fall down.'
2. Whatever was done, the fire was murder.
   - The old woman nods slowly. 'Both things are true,' she says. 'It is heavy, carrying both.'
3. I don't know what to think.
   - 'Honest,' says the old woman. 'Keep it that way. Sit.'

## 1.6  "The Runner"  (`runner`)

- **Starts when:** 4 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; Major Lvl 3 or more (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** Meet cinder (walk to their tile).  "Find Cinder Wraith near {@cinder}."
- **Pays:** nothing
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "cinder")`
- **Words:** 246 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The old woman gave you one more thing before you left, a description. 'The boy who lived. His sister carried him out and died of the water two years later. He ran off, and he never came back.'

A runner, Wen said. A grey cloak. Cinder Wraith.

You have been looking at your own life through a keyhole. Now you want the door.

Word has it he guards caravans near {@cinder}.

**Closing scene**

He is not what you pictured. He is lean and tired, with a runner's legs and a face like a closed door. He sits on a low wall, eating a cold dumpling, and he watches you come the whole way.

**Cinder:** You've got herb smoke on you. Azure Cloud. So one of you lived.

**You:** You burned it.

**Cinder:** I did.

*[only if mercy is 1]* **You:** I've been to Marrow Reach.

*[only if mercy is 1]* **Cinder:** Then you know why.

*[only if mercy is 2]* **You:** Whatever they did, the children in that kitchen did nothing.

*[only if mercy is 2]* **Cinder:** I never checked. That is the truth. I did not check.

*[only if mercy is 3]* **You:** I went to Marrow Reach. I still don't know what to think.

*[only if mercy is 3]* **Cinder:** That makes two of us.

**Cinder:** For years I told myself I would do it again. Lately I am less sure.

**Cinder:** But I won't talk to someone I can put down with one hand. I'm tired of running, so I won't run from you. If you want answers, come and take them.

He goes back to his dumpling. It is the most frightening thing anyone has ever done to you.

## 1.7  "The Torch"  (`torch`)

- **Starts when:** at once when the previous chapter ends
- **Task:** Defeat cinder (only you can kill them).  "Face Cinder Wraith and win."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **Words:** 343 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

He is a whole Major above you. You can feel it from here, like heat off a forge.

Train first, if you need to. He said he would wait, and he does not look like a man who lies about small things.

When you are ready, face him. Type 'attack' while you stand in the same place.

**Closing scene**

*[only if dead.cinder]* The fight is over. He slides down the wall and does not get up.

*[only if dead.cinder]* You go through his coat, because you have to. A child's wooden bird. A flask. A folded paper, stiff with old sweat, sealed in green wax with a leaf crest.

*[only if dead.cinder]* It is the same leaf as the letter on your table. 'Cinder, my boy. Make it complete. O.V.'

*[only if dead.cinder]* You stand over him a long time. The wind smells of rain. It does not feel like winning.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* He drops to one knee with a hand over his ribs. You hold your blade at his throat. Then you take it away.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* **Cinder:** Why?

*[only if not dead.cinder]* **You:** Because the one who paid you is still out there.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* He is quiet so long that you think he will not answer.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* **Cinder:** A man with a clean voice. He smelled of cedar and lamp oil. He gave me a torch and a green seal and told me Azure Cloud had poisoned my home. It was true. I believed him because it was true.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* **Cinder:** He took me in when I was nine. He fed me. He taught me to run. I called him uncle.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* His face changes slowly as he hears himself say it.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* **Cinder:** He was the one who bought the root. He was there the whole time.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* He looks like a man who has just seen his own house from the outside. 'Go,' he says. 'I need to go and sit with some graves.'

Cedar. Lamp oil. Green wax and a leaf crest. You think of a round, warm man pouring tea.

*[only if patron is 1]* Three thousand of his spirit stones are still in your pocket. They have never felt so heavy.

## 1.8  "The Ledger"  (`ledger`)

- **Starts when:** 2 year(s) after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Go to the place `vale`.  "Find proof in the records hall of {@vale}."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **Words:** 310 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Wen sets the green seal beside the burned ledger page, and neither of you speaks until the lamp needs trimming.

**Wen:** Orrin Vale.

*[only if patron is 1]* **Wen:** You took his money.

*[only if patron is 1]* **You:** I know.

*[only if patron is 1]* **Wen:** So did Hui, I think, for years. That is what we will have to live with.

*[only if patron is 2]* **Wen:** And you turned down his gold. I didn't understand why at the time. I do now. Good instinct.

**Wen:** We have a seal, and a story from a man who burned us. A magistrate will laugh at that. We need paper.

**Wen:** A man like that keeps copies. He keeps them in his own city, in a hall he walks past every night. Go and read them.

**Closing scene**

The records hall of {@vale} smells of dust and cedar oil. A tired clerk looks at your sect seal, looks at your face, and finds he suddenly needs to be somewhere else for an hour.

The Marrow Reach accounts fill a whole shelf. Silver for root, silver for wagons, silver for the men who 'managed the water.' Every page is stamped with the leaf.

Below it is a smaller book. Monthly payments to 'C.W.' for services. The last entry is a big one, dated the week of the fire.

At the bottom of the shelf lies a single folded letter. The ink is brown. You know the hand at once.

'Orrin. I have seen the water at Marrow Reach. I will not make another batch. On the first of the month I will write to the Provincial Court and tell them everything. I am sorry, old friend. I should have asked sooner. Hui.'

He had written the truth. He was one week from telling it. One week.

You sit down on the cold floor with the letter on your knees. You cry a little, quietly, the way you could not at the grave.

## 1.9  "The Last Cup"  (`cup`)

- **Starts when:** at once when the previous chapter ends
- **Task:** No task: the closing scene follows at once.
- **Pays:** nothing
- **When it closes, the code:** `(c, st) -> { Character o = Chapters.person(st, "orrin"); if (Chapters.flag(st, "orrin") == 1 && o != null) { o.fatedTo = 0; o.ss = 0; Chapters.set(st, "exposed", 1); } }`
- **Words:** 178 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

You are barely out of the hall when a servant finds you in the street. He is polite and out of breath.

**Servant:** The Magistrate asks if you would take tea. He says he has been expecting you.

The garden is the same garden. The tea is the same tea. Orrin Vale pours with the same careful hands, and he does not look surprised.

**Orrin:** You read my records. I wondered when you would. I kept the letters because I am a vain man. Hui's was the only one I could not bring myself to burn.

**You:** You killed forty people to hide a letter.

**Orrin:** I killed forty people to save a province's trade, and my own neck, and thousands of jobs that depend on that root. I am not asking you to like it.

**Orrin:** I am asking you to be practical. Marrow Reach is sixty graves. The fire is forty. Nothing will undo them. What is left is you and me, and a province that needs a steady hand. Sit beside me. I will make you very strong.

**Question after the opening scene** (kept as the flag `orrin`; default: option 1)

> What do you do?

1. Tell everyone. Send the records to the Court and to the people of Marrow Reach.
   - **Orrin:** They may hang me. Or they may bribe someone, and I will live in a smaller house. You cannot know which.
   - **You:** No. But they will know the truth.
   - You leave the cup untouched. Behind you, Orrin Vale begins, very softly, to hum.
2. Draw your weapon. This ends here.
   - **Orrin:** Hui's student. Of course.
   - He sets down the cup with great care, the way you set down a thing you will never lift again.
   - **Orrin:** I would rather not. But I will not make it easy.
3. Take his offer.
   - The tea is still warm. The records are still in your sleeve. You tell yourself it is only for now.
   - It is not only for now. In the years ahead you will grow very strong, and very comfortable, and you will stop looking at graves.
   - *[only if not dead.wen]* Wen leaves you at the city gate without a word. She does not turn around.

## 1.10  "The Reckoning"  (`reckoning`)

- **Starts when:** at once when the previous chapter ends; (left out altogether if `(c, st) -> Chapters.flag(st, "orrin") != 2`)
- **Task:** Defeat orrin (only you can kill them).  "Face Orrin Vale and win."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **When it closes, the code:** `(c, st) -> { Character o = Chapters.person(st, "orrin"); if (o != null && !o.dead) { o.fatedTo = 0; o.ss = 0; Chapters.set(st, "exposed", 1); } }`
- **Words:** 184 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Orrin Vale does not hide. He sits in the same garden with the same cup, and he waits for you with a sword across his knees.

He is stronger than you, and he knows every stone of this city. Train first, if you need to. He will not run.

When you are ready, face him. Type 'attack' while you stand in the same place.

**Closing scene**

*[only if dead.orrin]* He falls across the tea table and the cup breaks. For a moment he looks like what he is, a tired old man who made a mistake and then a worse one.

*[only if dead.orrin]* **Orrin:** I never wanted the fire. I wanted one more year.

*[only if dead.orrin]* There is no one to answer him. He is gone before you finish listening.

*[only if not dead.orrin]* He kneels with his sword on the stones. You leave him his life. You take his seal.

*[only if not dead.orrin]* By evening, the records are on their way to the Provincial Court, with his confession signed below them in shaking ink.

Marrow Reach gets its truth. It is not enough. But it is something to bury beside the dead.

## 1.11  "Those Who Loved Him"  (`avenger`)

- **Starts when:** 4 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; (left out altogether if `(c, st) -> Chapters.flag(st, "dead.cinder") == 0`)
- **Task:** Defeat pell (only you can kill them).  "Face Pell Wraith, who hunts you."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> { Character pell = Chapters.spawn(c, st, "pell"); Character w = Chapters.person(st, "wen"); }`
- **Words:** 240 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Four years pass. You grow stronger. You do not forget, but you stop counting.

Then, one morning, a note is nailed to your door.

'You killed the man who raised me when no one else would. I am coming. Pell Wraith.'

A second note comes with the first, from {@wen}. 'Someone came to the stall last night. I hit her with the scale. Don't worry. Wen.' You are not sure whether to laugh or be sick.

She has your name and a head start. Make her come to you, or go and meet her. Either way, it ends.

**Closing scene**

*[only if dead.pell]* She was fast, and angry, and very young, and you were not. When it is done, you find a small wooden bird in her pocket, the twin of the one you took from her uncle.

*[only if dead.pell]* You wonder who will carve the third.

*[only if not dead.pell]* She lies on her back in the dust, glaring at the sky. You sit down beside her. After a while you hand her Hui's letter and the green seal.

*[only if not dead.pell]* **Pell:** Then who did we kill?

*[only if not dead.pell]* **You:** Nobody who deserved it. Your uncle was told a half-truth by the man who made the other half. It was a good lie. It nearly worked twice.

*[only if not dead.pell]* She does not thank you. She does not forgive you. But she takes the letter, and in the morning she is gone, and the wooden bird is on your doorstep.

## 1.12  "A Letter From the South"  (`debt`)

- **Starts when:** 4 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; (left out altogether if `(c, st) -> Chapters.flag(st, "dead.cinder") != 0`)
- **Task:** No task: the closing scene follows at once.
- **Pays:** +3 potential
- **Words:** 104 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

A letter comes in a rough hand, from a village you visited once and have not stopped thinking about.

'I did what you said. I sat with the graves. Then I started clearing the creek. The bitterbell is gone and the water is mending, slowly. Last spring a child drank from it and did not get sick. I thought you should know. I don't ask for forgiveness. I only want you to know somebody is keeping the place. C.'

A small wooden bird is folded in the paper. Someone carved it long ago, and someone has kept it dry ever since.

## 1.13  "What a Sect Is For"  (`sect`)

- **Starts when:** 3 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; Major Lvl 3 or more (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** FOUND_SECT 0.  "Raise the sect again: found Azure Cloud."
- **Pays:** 5,000 spirit stones, 2 Potential Pills, a technique insight
- **Words:** 176 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Years have passed since the fire. You are no longer the frightened pill-maker who stood in the ashes.

The old field is overgrown now. Green things grow up through the black. You stand at the gate where the chimney still stands, and you think about what a sect is for.

*[only if not dead.wen]* **Wen:** You'd better build something. I'm too old to be homeless again.

*[only if dead.wen]* You think of Wen, who would have complained about the roof.

*[only if orrin is 3]* You have everything Orrin promised: a seat, a name, a city. It is not a bad life. It is only a life with a locked door in it that you walk past every day. Tonight you will unlock it.

**Closing scene**

The sign goes up on a bright morning. It is plain wood with a blue cloud painted on it, a little crooked, because you let a child hold the brush.

The cracked cauldron stands in the middle of the new courtyard. You look at it until the light changes. It has been with you through every part of this.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `cauldron`; default: option 1)

> What will you do with the cracked cauldron, and Master Hui's secret?

1. Mend it and make the Silent Tonic again, safely, and send the profit to Marrow Reach.
   - The smith says it can be done. It takes a month, and the new seam shines like a scar that has healed well.
2. Bury it in the herb garden beside Master Hui.
   - You dig the hole yourself. It takes all afternoon. When it is done, the garden looks as if nothing happened, which is how Master Hui would have liked it.
3. Hang it in the front hall, crack and all, so every new student sees it.
   - It takes four men and a rope. When it is up, it hangs a little crooked, and the light comes through the crack in a thin blue line.

## 1.I1  Interlude: The Chimney  (between season 1 and season 2)

**Interlude**

Azure Cloud is never going to be a great sect. It has thirty people, a herb garden gone half to seed, a kitchen roof that is mostly patch, and one chimney that nobody is allowed to take down. The sign over the gate hangs crooked. You gave up straightening it.

*[only if cauldron is 1]* The mended cauldron brews a pill that quiets a cough and does nothing else. Every spring a cart goes south to Marrow Reach with the profits, and every spring somebody sends back a jar of creek water with a ribbon round its neck.

*[only if cauldron is 2]* The cauldron lies in the herb garden under a plain stone, next to the master who liked to sit there. New students are not told why. They find out once they have been here long enough to ask the right question.

*[only if cauldron is 3]* The cracked cauldron hangs in the front hall. New students ask about it on their first morning, and you tell them the whole story, including the parts that make Azure Cloud look bad.

*[only if dead.cinder]* Cinder Wraith has a stone of his own in the yard, set a little apart. You are still not sure it was right. Every year you leave a wooden bird on it, and every year the bird is gone by morning.

*[only if not dead.cinder]* Cinder never joined the sect. But every spring a thin man in a grey cloak walks in at the gate, eats a bowl of noodles in the kitchen, and walks out again without a word.

*[only if exposed is 1]* Orrin Vale lived out his years in a smaller house, as he said he would, and wrote to you twice a year. You answered once.

*[only if dead.orrin]* Orrin Vale's seat in {@vale} stayed empty a long time. When it was filled, the new magistrate's first act was to pay for a well at Marrow Reach.

*[only if orrin is 3]* Orrin Vale never said the word Marrow in your hearing again. Neither did you.

*[only if not dead.wen]* Wen runs the herb garden and complains about everyone else's pruning, and nobody has asked {wen.him} to stop.

*[only if dead.wen]* Wen's stall in {@wen} was never sold. A girl from the noodle shop runs it now, and she has started stitching a small blue cloud on her sleeve.

Evenings, you sit in the herb garden where Master Hui liked to sit, and you tell him how it went. You don't expect an answer. For the first time in years you aren't sure he would have had one.

Meanwhile, at the market in {@wen}, a man with a very clean cart is handing out free samples of a tonic with a familiar name. Nobody at the sect has heard about it yet.

# 1.S2  Season 2: The Silent Tonic

## 1.14  "Thirty Beds and a Cow"  (`beds`)

- **Starts when:** 3 year(s) after the previous chapter ended; a wish: a sect with a few students in it (given up after 6 more years of waiting)
- **Task:** Make 6 items **since this chapter began**.  "Show Dunn how it is done: make six pills."
- **Pays:** 200 spirit stones
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> { Chapters.spawn(c, st, "dunn"); mark(c, st); }`
- **Words:** 392 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Three years of rebuilding have taught you that a sect is mostly plumbing. Azure Cloud now has thirty beds, two of which do not leak, a roof over the kitchen, and a waiting list that begins with a young man named Dunn, who has arrived at the gate with a cow.

**Dunn:** She's called Duchess. She hasn't got any talent, I'll say that straight out, but she's very loyal. I thought she could be, you know. The mascot.

**Wen:** We have a cat.

**You:** The cat will want to see her references.

Dunn wants to learn how to make pills the way they do in the stories, where a farm boy swallows one and sparks come out of his ears and a dragon is impressed. You explain that at Azure Cloud the pills are for coughs. He says that is fine. He says there is a lot of coughing at home.

Then, a moment later, he frowns, because that is not quite true. He says there used to be a lot of coughing at home. There has been none since the spring.

**Closing scene**

His first pill comes out the colour of a bruise and smells like a wet dog. His second is better, which is to say it is only a bruise. By the sixth, Duchess has eaten two of the failures with every sign of enjoyment and has not died, and Wen has declared that this is the sect's first clinical trial.

**Wen:** Don't look so pleased. I only said it was a trial. I didn't say it was a good one.

Wen is sitting on the end of the bench with a mortar in {wen.his} lap, grinding something that does not need grinding. {wen.He} has been here every evening for three years and has never once said why. You have never once asked. It is the kind of arrangement that two careful people can keep up for decades, if nobody drops a mortar.

**Dunn:** It's the quiet I mind, if I'm honest. The cough stopped, and the shouting stopped, and my uncle's leg is still broken, and he hasn't said a word about it since the spring. A man with a leg like that ought to complain. It's his right.

He says it like someone reporting a haunting. Nobody speaks for a moment. Duchess lows, once, at nothing in particular.

## 1.15  "Free Samples"  (`samples`)

- **Starts when:** 10 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Meet quay (walk to their tile).  "Speak to the salesman at the striped awning."
- **Pays:** 1 Cultivation Pill
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "quay")`
- **Words:** 305 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The man with the clean cart is easy to find, because he wants to be found. He has set up under a striped awning in the market at {@hide}, between a woman selling ribbons and a man selling the same ribbons at a different price. A hand-lettered board says SILENT TONIC, NEW FORMULA, SAMPLES FREE.

Dunn has gone pale. Wen has gone quiet, which in {wen.him} is worse. You take a sample bottle from the little tray, and for a second nobody is selling anything.

**Wen:** That's Hui's name for it. Nobody else ever called it that. It was never sold. It was never even written down, except in the iron.

**You:** Somebody wrote it down.

**Closing scene**

**Quay:** Pettibone Quay, of the Verdigris Guild, at your service and at a very fair price. You are the Azure Cloud people. Everyone says so. I have a standing instruction to be pleasant to you, which is a thing I rarely get to say about a customer.

**You:** Whose instruction?

**Quay:** My employer values discretion. I value my employer's valuing of it. Please, take a bottle. Take six. It does nothing at all.

He means it as a selling point. Wen unstoppers a bottle and tastes it off the tip of a finger and says nothing for a long moment, and then says something you will still remember when the bottle is long gone.

**Wen:** It is not poison. That's the horror of it. It does exactly one thing, and it does it well. It takes the complaining out of a body. The pain is still there, and the hunger is still there. Whoever drinks it just stops mentioning them.

Quay is still smiling, and you see that he does not know. He sells it the way a man sells salt. Somewhere further up the road there is somebody who does.

## 1.16  "The Quiet Farm"  (`farm`)

- **Starts when:** 6 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Go to the place `farm`.  "Go to Lower Hobb, at {@farm}."
- **Pays:** nothing
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "maud")`
- **Words:** 145 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

Dunn's village is called Lower Hobb, and it is the cleanest place you have ever seen. Every fence is mended. Every field is weeded. The children are in the fields at dawn, and there are no sounds at all but the hoes, which go up and down in time with one another like the oars of a very large, very slow boat.

A woman looks up as you come in. She does not wave. She goes on working. She has a bandage on her hand that has been wrapped, you would say, for about a week.

**Maud:** Visitors are welcome. We are well. Everyone is well. Thank you for asking.

You had not asked. Dunn has gone to find his uncle, and you stand there, beside a woman who has been well for a week with a bandage the colour of old tea.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `farmplan`; default: option 1)

> A whole village has stopped complaining. What do you tell them?

1. Tell them to stop drinking it.
   - **Maud:** And do what, when the harvest is in and my back is breaking? Sleep? I haven't slept right in six years. It was the first time I slept right, the spring that bottle came.
   - She is not angry. She says it like a fact about the weather. You find that you have nothing to say to it.
2. Offer to trade: honest pills for the bottles.
   - **Maud:** Pills for bottles. All right. But you'll want to be quick. The man comes on the first of the month, and the last time somebody turned his bottle away, the bottle came back, with a letter.
   - She does not tell you what was in the letter.
3. Say nothing yet. Watch, and count what they are not saying.
   - You count. It takes you the afternoon. Fourteen broken things, from a leg to a heart, and not one of them mentioned out loud. By evening you know the village by what it does not say, which is a kind of intimacy you would rather not have had.
   - **Wen:** You're doing the thing where you carry other people's silence around with you.
   - **You:** I'm not doing anything.
   - **Wen:** You are, and it's heavy, and I am going to sit next to you until you put it down.

## 1.17  "Ten Honest Pills"  (`honest`)

- **Starts when:** 2 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Make 10 items **since this chapter began**.  "Brew the rousing draught: make ten pills for the village."
- **Pays:** 300 spirit stones, gear a Major above you
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> mark(c, st)`
- **Words:** 361 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

There is no cure for a thing that is not a disease, but there is a way to wake a body up again. Wen finds it in the third of Hui's notebooks, the one you have been afraid to open. It is a long, patient recipe for something called a rousing draught, and in the margin, in a different ink, someone has written: 'Slow, or it hurts them.'

*[only if farmplan is 2]* **Wen:** Pills for bottles. Maud will keep her end. She seems like a woman who keeps her end.

*[only if farmplan is 1]* **Wen:** You told them to stop. They'll listen better if the thing you offer instead is not nothing.

*[only if farmplan is 3]* **Wen:** You counted fourteen. Brew fourteen, then, if you like. I'm told it's the reverse of counting sheep.

Brewing is slow work, and it is not glamorous. Nobody would put it in a story. It is the same motion, again and again, in a room that smells of crushed leaves, with a boy in the corner who has learned not to talk while the cauldron is turning.

**Closing scene**

The first one to wake up properly is Dunn's uncle. He sits up on the bed and looks at his broken leg as though someone has brought it in from the street. Then he says, to nobody, 'Oh, hell, that hurts.' Everybody in the room laughs, the kind of laughing that is mostly crying. It is the first complaint Lower Hobb has made in six months.

Maud waits until the end of the day. Then she goes to the back of the house and comes back with something wrapped in a cloth, and she sets it down in front of you as if it might bite.

**Maud:** This came with the bottles. They gave us a chit with every crate, because we aren't allowed to carry coin out of the village. It's stamped. You can have it. I don't want to know what it says.

It is a little slip of green paper. It says, in a printer's neat type, BY ORDER OF THE GREEN TABLE, and beneath that the name of the Factor, and beneath that a number, which is the village's quota of silence for the year.

## 1.18  "Old Hob Likes the Quiet"  (`hob`)

- **Starts when:** 10 weeks after the previous chapter ended

**Opening scene**

The rousing draught works on twelve of the thirteen people you try it on in Upper Hobb, which has the same name as Lower Hobb, a worse road, and a shop that sells nothing but thread. The thirteenth is a man called Hob.

He is seventy, and he sits on a bench in front of his house with his hands on his knees, looking at a view. It is a very good view: a hill, a stand of birches, a long gold slope of barley going down to a stream. He has had it for forty years. His neighbours say that since the spring he has not complained about anything, which is not like him. When Dunn holds out the cup he looks at it, and at Dunn, and says, quite kindly: 'No, thank you, lad.'

**Hob:** It's the first time in nine years that I've sat on this bench and not minded. I'd like to go on.

**Dunn:** But it's only the tonic. It isn't you. It's what it does to you.

**Hob:** I know what it does. Do you know what it does? It lets a man look at a hill.

**Closing scene**

*[only if hob is 1]* At dusk he takes the cup off the bench by himself, and looks into it, and does not drink. 'Ask me next week,' he says. It is the first thing he has asked of anyone in a year. You write it in the book Wen keeps, under H, and underline it twice.

*[only if hob is 2]* By nightfall he has wept himself out and is eating bread and cheese in the kitchen with the lamp lit. He is very angry with you. He is furious. He will go on being furious for a month, and then he will send you a small, bad painting of a hill.

*[only if hob is 3]* He talks for an hour. It is mostly about the paint: the lead white, the burnt umber, the ground-up lapis she saved for a year to buy and used on the sky of one single picture. When he finishes, he reaches for the cup, and holds it, and says: 'Not today. But I know where it is.'

On the road home, Dunn is unusually silent. At the crossroads he says: 'I wanted to be a hero. I thought it was mostly the fighting.'

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `hob`; default: option 1)

> Old Hob will not take the draught.

1. Respect it: leave the cup on the bench, and sit with him.
   - You sit. Neither of you says anything for the whole of the afternoon. Wen comes with a flask. Dunn, who cannot bear a silence, hums, and finds that the hill does not mind.
2. Wake him anyway. The tonic is a theft, even when he wants it.
   - **Hob:** You had no right.
   - **You:** No. I know.
   - He drinks it anyway, because you do not leave. The colour comes back into his face like a slow tide. He puts his hands over his eyes.
3. Ask him what he is not feeling, and let him say it.
   - **Hob:** My wife painted that hill. Forty summers. Every one a bit different. She died in the spring, and the first bottle came the same week, and it was like being handed a very large, very soft coat.
   - **You:** And if you took it off?
   - **Hob:** Then I'd have to know she was dead.

## 1.19  "What Orrin Kept"  (`kept`)

- **Starts when:** 1 year(s) after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Meet lisbet (walk to their tile).  "Meet Lisbet Vale, at {@hide}."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "lisbet")`
- **Words:** 450 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

You have heard the name Green Table before, once, in a margin of Orrin Vale's ledger, written very small. Back then it looked like a typing error.

*[only if dead.orrin]* Orrin is in the ground, and the records are in the Court's hands, and nobody has been able to tell you who the Table was. Then the letter comes, in a hand that is not his, and it begins: 'You do not know me. I am the reason he did it.'

*[only if not dead.orrin]* Orrin lives in a smaller house now, as he promised. He answers a letter from you after eleven days, which is the fastest he has ever answered anything. 'Come and see my daughter,' it says. 'She will not forgive me, and she is right. But she will talk to you.'

It is signed Lisbet Vale. She is waiting at {@hide}.

**Closing scene**

She is twenty-four, and she has her father's round cheeks and none of his ease. She keeps her back to the wall. She has a way of looking at a door as if it owes her money.

**Lisbet:** Everyone assumed my father was greedy. He was in debt. The province had a bad harvest, and the Green Table lent him the money to buy grain, and took me as surety. I was fourteen. I was a ward in their counting-house for four years. I learned to keep books. I learned them very well.

**Lisbet:** They said they only wanted one favour. Marrow Reach had a root that made the tonic. They wanted the tonic, a great deal of it, for the farms. A farm that does not complain is a farm that pays its rent. They called it a gentle policy. When your master found out and said he would write to the Court, there was only one more delivery to make, and I would have been free.

**Lisbet:** One more year. That was what he said to himself, I think. He said it on the night of the fire, and he said it as he signed the order. He thought he was buying my life.

*[only if not dead.orrin]* Behind her, in the corner, an old man you know sits on a stool with his hands between his knees, and does not look up. He has aged a decade in a handful of years.

**Lisbet:** I got out. They'll want me back. They'll want what I took: the Table's second set of books. It lists every farm, every quota, and every magistrate they own. If it were read out in a public court, nobody would be able to pretend any more.

**You:** And you want me to read it out.

**Lisbet:** No. I want you to steal the rest of it. I only took half.

## 1.21  "Wen Under the Pear Tree"  (`pear`)

- **Starts when:** 6 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Wait: nothing to do, the closing scene comes 1 weeks (0 years and 1 weeks) after the opening scene.
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **Words:** 375 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

There is a pear tree behind the herb garden that has never fruited. It was there when the sect was a field of ash, a thin black stick in the middle of the char, and it was the first thing to put out a leaf. Wen sits under it most evenings, with a bowl of something to peel, and a knife that is a good deal sharper than the work needs.

You sit down on the grass beside {wen.him}. You have done this a thousand times. Tonight {wen.he} puts down the bowl.

**Closing scene**

**Wen:** I was never a disciple, you know. People think so. I was the herbalist who brought the mint on Tuesdays. Hui used to give me tea in a cup with a saucer. Nobody had ever done that. I thought there must have been some mistake, and I kept coming back to see if it would be noticed.

**Wen:** After the fire I kept the stall for a year. I left the door unlatched every night. I told the neighbours it was for the cat. I thought, if the cloud-sleeve boy is alive, he'll need to be able to walk in.

{wen.He} says it to the peel in {wen.his} hands. The knife goes round, and the long green ribbon comes away in one piece, as unbroken as a sentence.

**Wen:** So when I say I don't mind about the plan, I want you to know that I'm not brave. It's that I've spent a year practising for you not coming back, and you did, and everything since has been a bonus. I'd walk into a counting-house for that. I'd walk into a lot of things.

You find that you want to answer, and cannot. What comes out instead is that the pear tree has never fruited. 'It's a male,' says Wen, calmly. 'It needs another one. Someone planted it on its own.'

You look at the tree. You look at {wen.him}. You say that it seems a pity. {wen.He} laughs, once, a short bright startled laugh. {wen.He} picks up the bowl again. There is a nursery in the next county, {wen.he} says, that sells a good female pear, and it would be a perfectly reasonable thing for two people to plant.

## 1.22  "The Plan, Version Two"  (`rehearse`)

- **Starts when:** 2 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Wait: nothing to do, the closing scene comes 2 weeks (0 years and 2 weeks) after the opening scene.
- **Pays:** nothing
- **Words:** 293 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

There is a way to find the holes in a plan, and it is to act it out in a kitchen with the wrong people. You push the table to the wall. Dunn is to play the Factor, because he is the only one who is not afraid of her. Duchess is the ice sculpture. Lisbet, who has actually met the Factor, is to give directions, and has taken one look at the cow and sat down on a stool with her face in her hands.

**Lisbet:** She doesn't walk like that. She walks as if she has never in her life been asked to wait for anything. Dunn, you are walking like a man looking for the privy.

**Dunn:** I am looking for the privy. The scene's been going twenty minutes.

**Closing scene**

By the fourth go, Dunn has got it. He has stopped walking like a farm boy and begun to move like something carved out of cream. He pauses in the doorway for exactly the right number of seconds. He looks round the room as if it were a small mistake he was prepared to forgive. When he speaks, it is in a low pleasant voice, and he says: 'A cousin from the provinces. How refreshing.'

There is a silence. Lisbet takes her hands from her face. She goes quite white. 'Do that again,' she says, and he does, and she says: 'No, don't. It's exactly her. I can't.'

**Wen:** He's very good.

**Dunn:** I think I might have been a duchess in another life.

Duchess, who has been standing in the middle of the kitchen as an ice sculpture for the whole of the evening and has not moved once, lowers her great head, and with enormous gentleness, eats the plan.

## 1.23  "Pettibone Quay Changes His Mind"  (`quayturn`)

- **Starts when:** 4 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Wait: nothing to do, the closing scene comes 2 weeks (0 years and 2 weeks) after the opening scene.
- **Pays:** 300 spirit stones, 1 Potential Pill
- **Words:** 481 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The salesman turns up at the sect gate on a wet evening with his cart, which is not clean any more, and a bottle in each hand. He has been walking for four days. He has the look of a man whose coat has been taken away and given back with something missing from the pockets.

**Quay:** I should like to speak to the person who gave Mrs. Maud Hobb of Lower Hobb a bottle of something that wasn't a tonic. Is it you? I have been trying to find her for a month. She sent a letter. It said, quite simply, I can feel my hands. Nobody has said anything like that to me in twenty years.

**Closing scene**

He sits in the kitchen with his hat on his knees and tells it badly, out of order, with the care of someone laying a table he has not laid before. He was a seller of hats, then of buttons, then of anything that could be put in a bottle. He took the Verdigris post for the pay. He did not ask what was in the tonic, because it was labelled, and because he had a wife in the south who was ill.

**Quay:** I have not been a good man. I would like to be considered a cheerful one. They are different, I know. But on the road from Lower Hobb to here, I counted. I have sold nine thousand four hundred and twelve bottles. I have a ledger. I wanted to know what I'd done, and I did the sums, and when I had finished I sat in a ditch.

Wen puts a bowl of soup in front of him without a word. He looks at it. He picks up the spoon as if it might go off. Dunn, who has said nothing at all, sits down next to him on the bench. The first thing, he says, is to eat. The second is to write it down. The third is to find out which villages. He says it exactly as the sect's old cook used to say it to the apprentices, when they had spilt something.

**Quay:** I have the route. I have every farm on it. I have the order of delivery, and the dates, and the name of every steward who signed. I should like to give it to somebody who can do something about it. I'd go myself, but I'm told I'm not trusted. I can't say I blame them.

He hands it over, in a leather book with a strap. It is worn at the corners. It is the most thorough thing you have ever seen: a hundred and eleven villages, in a clerk's cramped ink, each with a number beside it. The number is the quarter's quota of silence. Every one of them has been added up, and the total is underlined in red.

## 1.24  "A Plan, Told Twice"  (`plan`)

- **Starts when:** 8 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Go to the place `gala`.  "Go to the Green Table's gala, at {@gala}."
- **Pays:** nothing
- **Words:** 356 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The Green Table holds a gala once a year at its counting-house in {@gala}, to which the best-behaved magistrates of the province are invited. There will be music, and an ice sculpture of a plough, and the Factor herself in a gown with a train. And in the strongroom under the dance floor, behind a door that opens to one particular key, the other half of Lisbet's books.

The plan is Wen's, and it is a beautiful plan. You sit around the kitchen table, with the cat on the map to keep it flat, and listen to it twice.

**Wen:** One. Dunn comes in as a waiter. He is the one person here who looks harmless. Two. Lisbet is on the guest list under her mother's name, because they've never struck it off. She waits near the stairs. Three. You are the cousin from the provinces, and you are bored. Everyone believes in a bored cousin.

**Wen:** At the sixth bell, the ice plough falls over. That is a thing I will arrange. In the confusion, you go down to the strongroom, and Lisbet has the key, and it takes four minutes. Four. Not five. We are out the garden door before the first guest has been told to calm down.

**Dunn:** What am I doing with Duchess?

**Wen:** Duchess is staying here, Dunn.

**Dunn:** She'll be ever so upset.

**Closing scene**

The plan, as it turns out, was a thing that happened in the mind. In the room, the ice plough was delivered a day early and has started to melt across the dance floor. The waiters' uniforms were not cut for Dunn's shoulders. A magistrate who knew Lisbet's mother has recognised the name on the guest list and told everyone near him. And at the sixth bell the Factor herself, Ysolde Marr, in a green gown with a train that follows her like a rumour, walks up to you and offers you her arm.

**Marr:** A cousin from the provinces. How refreshing. Walk with me, cousin. I want to tell you what you are really doing here, and I would like to do it where we cannot be overheard.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `gala`; default: option 1)

> Ysolde Marr has your arm, and the strongroom is a floor below. How do you get the ledger?

1. Charm her. Keep her talking while Lisbet works the lock.
   - **Marr:** You are a fine liar. It is a pity that I am a better one. Still, it has been a long time since anybody tried flattery on me with such conviction. Let us see how far it goes.
   - It goes four minutes. It is exactly the four you needed, and you will not forget how you earned them.
2. Let Dunn's mistake become the distraction: the cow, and everything the cow implies.
   - Dunn, who is not a waiter, and who has not been told what to do with a cow, has done the single useful thing of his career: he has brought Duchess in through the garden doors. By the time the first magistrate has finished screaming, the gala has become a rodeo, and nobody has noticed the stairs.
   - **Wen:** I did not plan for the cow.
   - **You:** Nobody could have.
3. Skip the cleverness. Go down the stairs and take it.
   - The two guards at the head of the stairs are good at their jobs, and quite surprised. It is not a stealthy thing. It is the kind of thing that ends in the third act, with a lot of broken furniture, and the Factor's long, delighted laugh behind you.

## 1.25  "Duchess"  (`comeback`)

- **Starts when:** 1 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Wait: nothing to do, the closing scene comes 1 weeks (0 years and 1 weeks) after the opening scene.
- **Pays:** nothing
- **Words:** 263 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

There is a complication that the plan did not allow for, and it is in the doorway of the strongroom, eating a bale of the Factor's good cream-coloured velvet.

It is Duchess. She was told to stay at home, and did not. She followed the cart for eleven miles in the dark, came in behind the ice sculpture by the garden door, and has made her own arrangements. She turns her large placid head toward you and chews. The velvet is the colour of the Table's crest. It is, as far as you can tell, an heirloom.

**Closing scene**

**Wen:** I'm so sorry. I'm so very sorry. I told them. Dunn, I told you.

**Dunn:** She's got a mind of her own.

Thole stops in the corridor. He looks at the cow. He looks at the velvet. He has been a bodyguard for thirty years, and has been shot at, and stabbed, and once set on fire, and there is nothing in his training for this. He opens his mouth. Nothing comes. He closes it. He says, in a voice of immense, slow, bewildered gravity: 'That is a cow.'

**Lisbet:** She's very well behaved.

**Thole:** She is eating the Factor's curtains.

It is the one moment in your life you will see a man of that size consider the possibility that he might be in the wrong building. Duchess finishes the velvet, burps gently, and lies down across the doorway to the stair. She is not moving. There is nothing in the world that will move her. Thole, after a pause, takes off his hat.

## 1.26  "The Counting-House"  (`vault`)

- **Starts when:** 1 weeks after the previous chapter ended

**Opening scene**

The strongroom has a door as thick as a table and a lock that opens to a particular key, and Lisbet has it, on a chain around her neck, where she has kept it for six years. The door swings. Inside there are shelves, and on the shelves the other half of the books.

Between you and the shelves stands the Factor's bodyguard, Corvin Thole, a quiet man the size of a barn door, who has the manner of someone who has never been surprised in his life and is looking forward to it.

**Thole:** The Factor says nobody comes out. I don't ask why. I am paid to count the people who go in.

**Lisbet:** He taught me how to hold a pen.

**Thole:** That I did. Walk away from it, miss. I will make it quick.

**Closing scene**

*[only if dead.thole]* He goes down like a wall. The silence afterwards is the loudest thing you have ever heard. Lisbet kneels by him for a moment, with her hand over her mouth, and then gets up and starts to fill a sack with books.

*[only if not dead.thole]* He goes down on one knee, and you do not finish it. He looks up at you with something that might, in a more expressive man, have been gratitude. 'She was a good bookkeeper,' he says. 'The Factor will have my hide for this. Tell Lisbet to lock the door behind her. I won't follow.'

The books are heavy, and they are lovely, in a terrible way. Every farm, every quota, every magistrate with a price beside his name. Wen reads for a minute in the lamplight, and then closes the cover very carefully, the way you shut a door on a sleeping child.

**Wen:** There are four hundred villages in here.

**Opening scene**

The books go to the Provincial Court by three separate hands, and one of them is a magistrate who has just discovered how much of his income was owed to an upright citizen named Marr. It takes a month. Then it takes the whole province by surprise, which is a hard thing to do to a province.

The Green Table does not collapse. Institutions of that kind never do. But it becomes very quiet about itself. Ysolde Marr is seen in a coach at the border, and then she is not seen at all. Bottles of the Silent Tonic go on sale in a hundred markets for a week, at half price, and then they stop, because no one wants to be seen buying them.

**Closing scene**

*[only if lisbet_free]* Lisbet comes to stay for a season, and stays for six. She takes over the sect's accounts. In the first month she finds four mistakes. In the second she finds a fraud, which turns out to be Dunn's, and which turns out to be a cow he has been paying for out of the sect's treasury. She cannot stop laughing. It is the first time you have heard it.

On the evening the last of the news comes in, you and Wen sit on the roof of the kitchen with a bottle of Maud's cider. You can see the herb garden from here, and Hui's stone, and the lamp in the window of the room above the noodle shop that you shared once, when you had nothing, and thought that was all you would have.

**Wen:** I've been meaning to say something for three years. I've been meaning to say it every evening. I've rehearsed it on the cat.

**You:** What did the cat think?

**Wen:** The cat didn't think anything of it, which I took as encouragement.

**Question after the closing scene** (kept as the flag `love`; default: option 1)

> Wen has been waiting three years to say something.

1. Say it first: that you would like to stay, for good.
   - It comes out of you in about nine words, none of them good, and it turns out to be exactly enough. {wen.He} laughs, and then {wen.he} stops laughing, and then neither of you says anything at all for a little while, which turns out to be the best conversation you have ever had.
   - Down in the yard, the cat takes up its post on the wall. It has been waiting for this.
2. Let Wen say it, and answer honestly.
   - {wen.He} says it. It is not eloquent. It begins with a word about mortars and ends with a word about the roof. You tell {wen.him} what you would say, which is the same thing in a different order, and the cider goes warm in the bottle while you talk.
   - Down in the yard, the cat takes up its post on the wall. It has been waiting for this.
3. Say you are not ready, and that you would like to be.
   - **Wen:** That's all right. I've waited three years. I can wait a little more. I just wanted you to know there's a door, and it's open, and I'm the sort of person who can stand in a doorway through a whole winter.
   - You believe {wen.him}. That is the thing about Wen. You always do.

## 1.I2  Interlude: Five Years Later  (between season 2 and season 3)

**Interlude**

Azure Cloud has sixty beds, a proper roof, and a reputation. The reputation is for being the sect whose pills cure what the guild's pills only quiet.

*[only if e.spouse]* Wen is with you in the mornings now, and in the evenings, and there is a second toothbrush on the shelf over the basin that nobody thought to count, and nobody has complained.

*[only if not e.spouse]* Wen is still the person you tell things to, last thing at night, through a door that stays open.

*[only if dead.thole]* There is a small stone for Corvin Thole beside the kitchen steps. Lisbet put it there. She says it is the only stone in the sect that doesn't have a story attached, and she wants to keep it that way.

*[only if not dead.thole]* Corvin Thole came to the gate one winter, alone, and asked if the sect needed a man who could lift things. It did. He teaches the children how to fall.

The cat is a very old cat. Duchess is a very old cow. The cauldron sits in its new place of honour, and the people who live around it do not talk much about how long it has been since anyone used it.

One morning, a young man comes up the road with a basket on his arm, and a letter in his sleeve, and the nervous manner of someone who has been told to be polite. He stops at the gate. He looks up at the crooked sign. The letter is sealed with a candle, put out.

# 1.S3  Season 3: What the Cauldron Is For

## 1.28  "A Wick at the Gate"  (`wick`)

- **Starts when:** 5 year(s) after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Meet ambrose (walk to their tile).  "Hear what Ambrose has to ask of you."
- **Pays:** 300 spirit stones
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> Chapters.spawn(c, st, "ambrose")`
- **Words:** 373 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The young man is called Ambrose, and he is a Wick of the Outer Court, which means that at the Palace of the Oldest Order he is a candle somebody has not got round to lighting. He has walked eleven days with a lunch his mother packed, and he is, in a way he is clearly trying to hide, terrified of you.

**Ambrose:** I have a message. It's from the, well, from the Master of the Palace. I know he doesn't have a name. He didn't give one. He wrote this himself, which the Elders say has never happened, and I was told to say please.

The letter is short. It is in a hand that looks like somebody learning to write with their off hand. 'I am not allowed to say why. I am allowed to ask. Please keep the cauldron safe. Please do not let anyone take it. I am sorry about the please. I do not have many people to ask. ???'

**Wen:** He signed it with three question marks.

**Ambrose:** He does that. We all just call him Master. It's easier.

The cauldron is where you left it, in the front hall, by the door. It has sat there for years, and the crack in its belly has never grown, but this morning the light coming through it is a slightly different colour, as though the crack were looking out at something.

**Closing scene**

Ambrose will not say much more. He does say that Master Hui was a Wick once, long ago, in the pill kitchen of the Palace, and one of the best. He left on a night nobody talks about. The cauldron went with him, which is not the sort of thing that is meant to happen to a Palace's cauldron.

**Ambrose:** They say he left because he found out what the kitchen cooked. I'm not supposed to know that. I don't know what it was. I only know the pills in the Outer Court all taste a bit like pennies, and nobody asks.

You think about a small, pale man in a herb garden, patient as a stone, who said that a cauldron learns the hand that stirs it. You think about what he might have learned.

## 1.29  "Ambrose Unpacks"  (`unpack`)

**Opening scene**

Ambrose has never had a room of his own. At the Palace the Wicks of the Outer Court sleep in long rows, thirty to a hall, with their boots under their beds, in a smell of old straw and boiled cabbage. The room the sect gives him is the one over the stable. It has a window, a bed, a peg, and a mouse. He stands in the doorway with his bundle in his arms and looks at it as though it might be taken back.

**Ambrose:** Is it all mine? The whole of it?

**Dunn:** It's got a mouse. You'll want to talk to the mouse. He's reasonable.

**Closing scene**

He learns the sect in the way a person learns a language, by mistakes. He calls Wen 'honoured elder' and is told to stop. He bows to the cat. He eats the whole of a dumpling in two bites, at his first meal, and looks up in alarm, and finds that the whole table has been waiting for him to do it.

Dunn teaches him to milk Duchess. It takes an afternoon and goes as these things do. At the end, Ambrose is covered in milk to the ears and Duchess wears a fixed look of long-suffering dignity. Dunn, doubled up on an upturned bucket, says it is the best thing he has seen since the cow came to the gate.

That night Ambrose writes to his mother on a page torn from a recipe book. You see it later, left open on the peg. 'Dear Mother. I am well. I have been given a bed. There is a mouse in it. The people here eat at the same table as their Master. I do not know what to make of it. I have decided to make a great deal of it. Your loving son, A.'

## 1.30  "The Cellar Under the Grave"  (`cellar`)

- **Starts when:** 10 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Make 12 items **since this chapter began**.  "Cook from Hui's book: make twelve pills with nothing in them that hurt anybody."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill, a technique insight
- **When it opens, the code:** `(c, st) -> mark(c, st)`
- **Words:** 372 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The herb garden has a loose flagstone, you remember it now, by Hui's stone, where you have knelt a hundred times. This time you lift it. Underneath there are eleven steps going down and a cellar that smells of dry paper and old root.

He has left you a library. There are thirty notebooks, a lamp that lights itself when you step on the sixth stair, and a long table with a place laid at it, for one, with a cup and a cloth. It is the neatest thing you have ever seen. It is so much like him that you have to sit down on the stairs.

The first notebook is a recipe book. It is called, on the spine, in his handwriting, THINGS THAT HURT NOBODY. Each recipe has the same note at the bottom: 'Nothing here came from the dead.' He has underlined it twice.

**Wen:** He must have been trying to make up for something. A whole life of it.

**Ambrose:** Do you think he would mind if I read?

**You:** I think he would mind if you didn't.

**Closing scene**

The twelfth is the first that works. You feel it before you see it: a faint warmth in the iron, a sound in the crack like someone breathing out. The pill that comes out is the colour of the sky at the end of an afternoon. It tastes of absolutely nothing, which you gradually realise is the point.

In the last notebook, tucked in the back cover like a pressed flower, there is a single sheet. 'The Palace kitchen cooks the dead. Not cruelly. They are brought up from a place under the floor, and a pill is made, and the pill is given to the living, to help them climb. I was a cook there for nine years before I understood. I took the cauldron because it is the one that does it. I broke it so that it could not. If I am wrong, forgive me. If I am right, then the crack is not damage. It is a door.'

**Ambrose:** I didn't know. I swear I didn't.

**Wen:** None of us did. That's the sort of knowing that doesn't let you sit down for a bit.

## 1.31  "What Hui Cooked"  (`huiletter`)

- **Starts when:** 6 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Wait: nothing to do, the closing scene comes 1 weeks (0 years and 1 weeks) after the opening scene.
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill, a technique insight
- **Words:** 394 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

The last notebook has a letter in the back that is still unread. You found it on the second night and put it away, the way you put away a thing you are not yet strong enough to hold. Now you take it out and read it at the long table in the cellar, with Wen on one side and Ambrose on the other and the lamp that lights itself turned low.

It begins: 'To whoever stirs next.'

**Closing scene**

'I do not know your name. I hope you are kind, and I hope you are stubborn, and I suspect you will be the second more than the first. I was a cook in the Palace kitchen for nine years. I was good. I never asked what the pills were for. A cook does not. A cook asks whether the salt is right.'

'On the night I understood, I was alone in the kitchen with the big pot on and the pipes humming, and a man came down the corridor with a lamp. A plain man in an apron, who was not supposed to be there, who is never supposed to be anywhere. I knew who he was. Everyone does, and nobody says. He stood at the door. He looked at the cauldron, and at me, and at the hammer in my hand. I thought: he will stop me.'

'He put out his lamp. That is all. He stood in the dark in the corridor and he let me go by with the pot on my shoulder, and he did not say a word. I have thought about it every day for forty years. I do not know what it cost him. I know that he is the loneliest person who ever lived, and that he did this one thing on his own.'

'If you are reading this, he may have asked you for the cauldron. If he asks, say yes. If he does not, say yes anyway, and tell him I never forgot the lamp. Hui.'

**Ambrose:** He put the lamp out.

**Wen:** He did.

**Ambrose:** I thought it was just a thing they said. I thought it was a story, about the Master being kind.

You close the notebook. The lamp on the table, which lights itself, burns a little brighter, as if somebody had come in from the corridor.

## 1.32  "Mister Snuff"  (`snuff`)

- **Starts when:** 10 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Meet snuff (walk to their tile).  "Speak with the man at the gate."

**Opening scene**

He comes to the gate on a wet evening, a tall and very tidy man in a grey coat and a hat, carrying a long brass instrument that looks like a candle-snuffer, and which is not. He has the face of somebody who has been very polite his whole life, because it saved him effort. He knocks, three times, with the knuckle of one finger.

**Snuff:** I do hope I'm not intruding. I have been asked to collect an object. I've been told you have it. A cauldron, cracked, with a certain sort of seam. It isn't yours, you understand. It was never anyone's. It was lent, once, to a person who should have been more careful with it.

**You:** Who asked you?

**Snuff:** Oh, I couldn't say. They don't have a name. They have a talent for making rooms go quiet, and for not asking twice.

The air has the feeling of the end of a candle. When he smiles, it is like watching a window go dark one pane at a time.

**Closing scene**

He is very civil. He declines tea, and accepts a stool. He explains that the thing in your hall is dangerous to everyone, including its owners, because it has a hole in it, and the hole goes somewhere, and the place it goes is looking back. He says it as a kindness. He says it as if you were a child with a lit match.

**Snuff:** I am not here to harm you. Please believe it. I am here to put the lamp out before it burns the house. You may keep your sect, your friends, and every pill you like. I will leave you the garden. I only want the iron.

You look at the cauldron. You look at the crack, and the light coming through it, which has gone from the colour of the end of an afternoon to something pale and a little afraid. It seems, you think, to be listening.

**You:** I'll think about it.

**Snuff:** Of course. I shall wait. I am extremely good at waiting. It is, in fact, rather the whole of my profession.

## 1.33  "The Pill Kitchen"  (`kitchen`)

- **Starts when:** 6 weeks after the previous chapter ended
- **Task:** Go to the place `kitchen`.  "Go to the Palace of the Oldest Order, at Originis, and see its kitchen."
- **Pays:** 1 Potential Pill
- **Words:** 465 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

If you want to know what a cauldron is for, you can ask the cauldron's makers. The Palace's pill kitchen is on the lowest floor of the Outer Court, behind a door nobody notices, and it is the cleanest place you have ever seen. The floor is stone. The pans are polished. Along the north wall, a row of iron pipes goes down into the dark.

Ambrose has got you in on a delivery, in a sack of onions. It is the first time you have laughed since the gate.

The Palace does not ask your name. The cook on duty, a thin woman with her sleeves rolled up, takes one look at you and the onions and says, 'The soup's in the pot,' and walks away. It is a very good soup.

**Closing scene**

He is sitting at the cook's table when you look up, as if he had always been there. He is an ordinary man, of no age, in plain clothes, with a bowl in front of him. He holds the spoon the way a person holds a thing he has just learned to use. You know him at once. You have never seen him in your life.

**???:** I am not allowed to tell you who I am. That one I can keep. I can tell you that I like the soup. It is very good, isn't it? I have it every day. It is one of the things I like most about being here.

**???:** I can show you the pipes. I am allowed to show. They go down to the place where the Garden puts everyone it has finished with. People ask, sometimes, what happens to the dead. The answer is that they are used. It is not unkind. It is not kind either. It is a system. I am the system's reflection. I did not choose it.

**You:** Master Hui took the cauldron.

**???:** He was my best cook. I did not stop him. I want you to know that. I could have, and I stood in the corridor with the lamp out, and I let him go past. I have never told anyone. I think it may have been the first thing I ever did on my own.

He puts down the spoon. For a moment there is a shift in the room, a quiet slippage, like a sleeper turning over.

**???:** Mister Snuff is not mine. Mister Snuff is from the other side of the sky. If you give him the iron, I do not know what he will do with it. If you do not, I do not know what he will do to you. I am sorry. I have a great many things to be sorry about, and I seem to have collected a new one.

## 1.35  "A Cup of Cold Tea"  (`parley`)

- **Starts when:** 2 weeks after the previous chapter ended

- **Words:** 430 in the two scenes

**Opening scene**

He sends a note first. It comes on a salver, by a small grey boy, who sets it down on the kitchen table and goes away without being tipped. It is written on very good paper in a very upright hand. It says: 'I should like to explain myself before I am obliged to be rude. I shall be at the old stone bridge at dusk. I shall bring my own tea. Snuff.'

**Wen:** You're not going.

**You:** I am going.

**Wen:** Then I am coming and standing behind a tree.

**Closing scene**

He is sitting on the parapet with a flask and two tin cups, in his grey coat, with his hat beside him. The light is going. The stream under the bridge is making a small quick noise. He pours the tea without a word, and holds out a cup, and you take it, because it would be graceless not to.

**Snuff:** It is cold. I apologise. I find it keeps better. I am told that the dead prefer it.

**Snuff:** I should like to tell you what I am. It will save a good deal of unpleasantness. I do not belong to a country, or a creed. I belong to a very large and very old and extremely tired company, which has asked, over the course of a long time, a single question: whether the Garden is worth the trouble.

**You:** And you decided that it isn't.

**Snuff:** I did not decide. I was given a lamp-snuffer. I was not given the wish to be cruel. I put out the ones that are about to be put out in any case. That is all I do. I would be glad if you would believe it.

You drink the tea. It is very bad. Behind the willow, forty yards off, there is a small noise like someone stepping on a twig and trying to look as if they hadn't.

**Snuff:** What I cannot tell you is why the cauldron matters. I am not told. I am told only that it is a door, and that doors are the thing we are paid to close. It is not malice. It is, if you will believe me, a sort of housekeeping.

**You:** Housekeeping.

**Snuff:** It is a very large house. It has been open a very long time. Someone must go round at night, and see to the windows.

He finishes his tea. He shakes out the cup. He puts it back in the flask, and the flask in his coat, and stands, and bows. 'I shall come on Thursday,' he says. 'I shall try to be brief.'

The cauldron is not yours. This is the first thing that is said at the meeting, and it is said by Dunn, who has never in his life said anything first. He stands up on the bench in the sect hall with his hands in his sleeves. It seems to him, he says, that if it is going to be used for what it is going to be used for, then everybody ought to have a say.

So the sect sits down together. All seventy-one of them, on the benches and the floor and the window ledges, with Ambrose at the back looking as if he might be sent away at any moment, and Lisbet taking minutes, and Wen at the stove. There is one item on the sheet. It says: WHAT WE SHOULD DO WITH A DOOR.

**Closing scene**

The debate takes four hours. A girl of twelve, who has been at the sect for a month, points out that the cauldron has been in the hall for years and no one has ever asked it what it wanted. A grey old pill-grinder says that in his experience a door is a thing that you either shut or open, and that a person who stands in it is a draught. A boy of nine asks if the dead have to go anywhere, and is told by an old woman at the back, quite gently, that some of them would rather not.

**Wen:** Hui would have hated the meeting. He'd have gone to the garden. And then he'd have come back at the end and said something short, and we'd all have felt rather silly.

The vote, when it comes, is not on the question that was set. Dunn proposes it. He proposes that the sect decide not what to do with the door, but how to decide. Whoever stirs the cauldron should be allowed to choose, he says, and the rest of them should stand behind that person and hold the lamp.

It is carried by a show of hands, seventy to one. The one is Ambrose, who has not voted for anything in his life, and has put up his hand by mistake, and cannot work out how to put it down. Duchess, at the back, who has been allowed into the hall for the occasion, abstains.

**Lisbet:** I shall record it as unanimous.

**Ambrose:** I didn't mean to!

**Lisbet:** That's what unanimous means.
